purpose: Test whether the near-water-table gradient information identified by BC2-B4 can be recovered from the existing single moving-layer storage state and geometry, without adding a state variable or fitting a boundary coefficient.
hypothesis: The main qH defect is nonlinear averaging: psi(theta_bar) is not the boundary-relevant gradient. A one-parameter linear suction profile whose integral water storage exactly equals Wm may recover a physically meaningful boundary gradient from Wm and L alone.

profile_reconstruction.coordinate: x=H-z, x=0 at water table and x=L at the 90-cm anchor
profile_reconstruction.slope_solution: unique monotone root for a, solved by deterministic bisection with expanding nonnegative upper bracket
profile_reconstruction.hydrostatic_property: For exact hydrostatic storage Wm=integral theta(x) dx, a=1 and qH=0 exactly up to quadrature/root tolerance.

reference_evaluation.source: qualified BC2-A2 accepted projected Wm,H states
reference_evaluation.time_alignment: trapezoidal average of endpoint candidate qH versus interval-average accepted Reference qH
comparators: POINT_2_5CM full-order local-information diagnostic from BC2-B4, reported only as diagnostic context

adjudication.support_rule: The storage-consistent linear-profile closure receives operator support only if RMS and mean-absolute qH error are both lower than MOVING_LAYER_AVERAGE and sign-mismatch count is no greater in both WATER_TABLE_RISING and WATER_TABLE_FALLING strata, while HOLD is noninferior.
adjudication.local_information_gap_rule: Report how much error remains relative to the frozen POINT_2_5CM diagnostic; no requirement to match it is imposed.
